captions_meta.hook: POV: you sent your press release as a PDF attachment 📎😶
lines: Download → open → copy-paste. Every extra step costs you.
69% of journalists prefer pitches under 200 words (Muck Rack, 2025).
✓ Release text in the email body
captions_meta.li_hook:
A small habit that stops good releases being read: sending them as PDF attachments.
It sounds trivial. The impact isn't.
li_body: Muck Rack's State of Journalism 2025 found 69% of journalists prefer pitches under 200 words. Journalists want to decide quickly, without extra steps.
A PDF attachment adds three of them: download, open, copy. Pair it with a generic subject line and the odds of being read drop sharply.
li_points: Paste the release text straight into the email body.
Use the release headline as the subject line.
Share photos and supporting documents by link.
If you use a distribution platform, make sure the release lives on a web page that can be accessed and quoted.
captions_meta.li_close: Does your organisation still insist on PDFs because they look "more official"? Tell us below.
captions_meta.fb: Who still sends press releases as PDF attachments? 😅 Watch to the end for a version journalists actually prefer.
